message:
Thanks. I'll ask a few quick questions to see what you may qualify for. Please answer each one:

1. How many people live in your household, including you and your dad? (1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 or more)
2. Roughly how much does the household earn from work in a year, before tax? (none / $1 to $10,000 / $10,000 to $20,000 / $20,000 to $30,000 / $30,000 to $40,000 / $40,000 to $50,000 / $50,000 to $60,000 / $60,000 to $80,000 / $80,000 to $100,000 / $100,000 to $150,000 / $150,000 or more)
3. How much Social Security does your dad (or anyone in the household) get in a year? (none / $1 to $10,000 / $10,000 to $20,000 / $20,000 to $30,000 / $30,000 or more)
4. Any other yearly income, such as pensions, unemployment, interest, or child support? (none / $1 to $5,000 / $5,000 to $15,000 / $15,000 or more)
5. Roughly how much is in bank accounts and investments? (under $2,000 / $2,000 to $5,000 / $5,000 to $20,000 / $20,000 to $100,000 / $100,000 or more)
6. Does anyone have a disability? (no / yes)
7. Does anyone get health insurance through a job? (no / yes)
reply: Me and my partner. Very little, it's part time. We don't get any. We don't have any of that. We don't have any of that. Yeah. I'd have to check.

summary: New York household with no children. Your dad (72) lives with you, which makes him eligible to be screened for aged programs. Work income is very low (part time), and the household gets no Social Security or other income. Recommended: SNAP (low income, senior member, NY rules); Medicaid (low income in NY, including the aged pathway for your dad); SSI for your dad (age 65+, no income reported, but the asset limit must be confirmed). Not recommended: WIC, CHIP, TANF, child tax credit, and school meals, since there are no children and no pregnancy. Left open for a caseworker: EITC (depends on your age and exact earnings, which weren't confirmed), ACA premium tax credit (depends on whether anyone has job-based insurance and on the final Medicaid outcome), and the household size and marital status (answers were unclear, and the partner's status needs confirming). Savings were not clearly confirmed, so the caseworker should verify the asset limits for SSI and Medicaid.
